scope: Full prepared property VM increment R2 against native value-entry R2; original Owner/Scope/manifest/service/model causal paths inspected. Separate optional Torah View increment belongs to native peer/root review.

findings.title: Retained VM can lose its subscription during cancellation and immediate reattachment
causal_interleaving: Original SwiftUI view retains the model in @State and calls setupSubscriptions from .task.
Old invocation waits in the async publisher; disappearance cancels that task.
A new visible invocation may enter before the cancelled predecessor resumes its defer.
R1 active-bool guard makes the new invocation return; old defer then clears active and cancels the read, leaving no active subscription.
correction: R2 replaces the active boolean with a per-invocation passive UI subscription UUID and does not reject a valid new invocation because a cancelled predecessor has not unwound.
The old defer always removes its own observer but changes shared subscription/task state only if it still owns the current UUID.
Old notification callbacks, publisher iterations and result publication check that same UUID.
Both the cancellation check after the awaited canonical read and the exact current ParsedProperties comparison remain before publication.
The UUID grants no source/account/document/RPC or permission authority.

causal_review: Prepared initialization and canAddProperty return before the legacy Pinkha policy/cache path; setupSubscriptions selects a separate prepared path.

Prepared rebuild performs the original account/source-bound canonical read through loadModalPropertyIdentity and the original concrete manifest/search service; no bootstrap/save/cache adoption is added.
The newly created rebuild Task is outside the local temporary synchronous read scope. Rebuild publication re-enters the original current-source/instance scope.
The original PropertiesSectionBuilder remains the renderer input builder; internal/native property filtering uses the same identity snapshot and scope.

Removal reserves the original scheduleDocumentAction before Task creation, retains inherited named action permissions, reads canonical identity, then verifies byte-exact property ID/key and current original Property equality.

The original concrete PropertiesService and ObjectRelationDelete call remain the sole removal implementation; the call executes after the temporary read scope has returned to its reserved mutation lineage.
Original Owner admission, actual Invocation permit/currentness, account drain, cancellation/failed-write semantics and read-to-write restrictions are unchanged.
The previous native value-entry implementation and legacy setup/rebuild/removal/rest suffixes remain byte-identical.
